topic: Secondary prevention after stroke or TIA

audits.title: Secondary prevention for stroke in the United Kingdom: results from the National Sentinel Audit of Stroke.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians Intercollegiate Stroke Working Party audit standards
audits.setting: 235 hospitals in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (National Sentinel Audit of Stroke)

cycle1.result: 24% with previous cerebrovascular disease not on antithrombotic at admission; 9% of appropriate patients not on antithrombotic at discharge; 64% had lipids measured, with 36% of those with high cholesterol or LDL untreated.

audits.other_findings: Patients with more severe disability were more often not on antithrombotic (18% vs 8%); older patients were less likely to receive lipid lowering.
audits.citation: Rudd AG, Lowe D, Hoffman A, Irwin P, Pearson M. Secondary prevention for stroke in the United Kingdom: results from the National Sentinel Audit of Stroke. Age Ageing. 2004;33(3):280-286. doi:10.1093/ageing/afh107. PMID: 15082434.

audits.title: Does a higher 'quality points' score mean better care in stroke? An audit of general practice medical records.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians stroke guidelines for primary care; QOF stroke quality points
audits.setting: Two general practices, one in southwest London and one in Surrey

cycle1.result: Practice A scored 93.5% (29/31) of QOF stroke points; practice B 73.4% (22.75/31) but better RCP adherence: assessed in secondary care 96% vs 79% (P=0.001); seen same day 64% vs 44%; rehabilitation 56% vs 37%.

audits.other_findings: Higher QOF quality points did not reflect better adherence to RCP guidance.
audits.citation: Williams PH, de Lusignan S. Does a higher 'quality points' score mean better care in stroke? An audit of general practice medical records. Inform Prim Care. 2006;14(1):29-40. doi:10.14236/jhi.v14i1.612. PMID: 16848964.

audits.title: Secondary stroke prevention: practice patterns in a tertiary care stroke service.
audits.standard: Achievement of therapeutic targets or appropriate therapy for four secondary prevention interventions
audits.setting: Stroke service, University of Alberta Hospital (tertiary)

cycle1.result: Antithrombotic 92% [174/190]; antihypertensive 95% [136/143]; lipid lowering 68% [107/158]; smoking cessation 27% [17/64].

audits.citation: Fan JC, Mysak TM, Jeerakathil TJ, Pearson GJ. Secondary stroke prevention: practice patterns in a tertiary care stroke service. Can J Neurol Sci. 2010;37(2):245-251. doi:10.1017/s0317167100010003. PMID: 20437937.

audits.title: Secondary prevention of stroke: an evidence-based clinical audit in the primary care.
audits.standard: Evidence-based audit criteria and performance standards from literature review
audits.setting: General Outpatient Clinic, Hospital Authority, Hong Kong

cycle1.result: Marked deficiencies in cardiovascular risk assessment; satisfactory control in 47% of hypertensive (BP), 45% of diabetic (glucose) and 37% of dyslipidaemic (lipids) patients.

cycle2.result: BP control 73% of hypertensive patients; adequate metabolic control 62% of diabetic patients; significant improvements.

audits.citation: Chen CX, Chan SL, Law TC, Choi SK, Chan KH. Secondary prevention of stroke: an evidence-based clinical audit in the primary care. Hong Kong Med J. 2011;17(6):469-477. PMID: 22147317.

audits.title: An audit of the pharmacological management of ischaemic stroke patients in a metropolitan Australian hospital.
audits.standard: National Stroke Foundation Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management
audits.setting: Large teaching hospital, Peninsula Health (Frankston Hospital), Melbourne

cycle1.result: Discharged on antihypertensives 71%, lipid-lowering agents 67%, antithrombotics 85%.

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest pharmacist input in the multidisciplinary team may improve adherence further.
audits.citation: Khalil V, Li M, Hua QA. An audit of the pharmacological management of ischaemic stroke patients in a metropolitan Australian hospital. Int J Clin Pharm. 2015;37(1):8-11. doi:10.1007/s11096-014-0035-6. PMID: 25394833.

audits.title: Appropriate secondary prevention of stroke and transient ischaemic attack with antithrombotics: an audit in general practice.
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on secondary prevention of stroke/TIA
audits.setting: New Queen Street and Stanground Surgeries, Peterborough

cycle1.result: 234/236 post-stroke/TIA patients received antithrombotic therapy unless contraindicated.

audits.other_findings: Of 13 not on antithrombotics, bleeding risk was the reason in 10, no documented reason in 2; documentation of reasons was poor.
audits.citation: Williams I, Smith W, Nash E, Patel A. Appropriate secondary prevention of stroke and transient ischaemic attack with antithrombotics: an audit in general practice. Br J Gen Pract. 2020;70(suppl 1):bjgp20X711641. doi:10.3399/bjgp20x711641. PMID: 32554685.
